# Logical-picture and timestamp-window qualification

Recorded run results and output filenames below describe the measured historical
epoch. Generated reports/logs were removed from the current tree; see
[qualification and historical recovery](../../../../docs/plans/native-video-noncuda-audit.md#artifact-policy-and-historical-evidence).
Fixture inputs and independent reference oracles remain checked in.

This corpus compares reference preservation, with no application relevance labels.
The eight video cases cover default and explicit VFR selection, completed PAFF
field pairs, VP9/AV1 timestamp selection and two separate windows of the same
52-second Sintel clip. Two text queries also exercise cosine rankings/top-k.

`vfr.mov` is generated by
`video_policy_qualification.variants(video-mjpeg.mov)["vfr_average_fps"][0]`.
The compressed JPEG samples are unchanged; its stts durations are
`[1024,1024,1024,1024,8192,8192,6144,6144]` at the pinned source timescale.
Other corpus rows reference existing checked-in clips and their provenance.
Every source is SHA-256 pinned. PAFF has eight transport packets and four logical
pictures; FFprobe counted decoded pictures provide the independent reference.
FFmpeg does not decode the JM data-partition fixture correctly, so it is excluded
from this pretrained corpus; native logical indexing is checked against its
four-picture official JM oracle in the library suite.

The timestamp oracle reads FFprobe presentation-picture timestamps, sorts them
and searches exact rational targets independently of the native selection code.
Pinned PyTorch receives selected pixels with `do_sample_frames=False`. Default
sampling continues to use the pinned HF processor. JPEG RGB uses Pillow/libjpeg;
other clips use streamed FFmpeg RGB. Tool dependencies are qualification-only.

From the worktree root, with pinned checkpoint weights and the qualification
Python environment installed:

```sh
python tools/embeddinggemma2/video_compare.py --backend cpu \
  --corpus tools/embeddinggemma2/testdata/sampling/corpus.json \
  --model-dir .benchmark-assets/native-video/model \
  --output /tmp/sampling-pytorch.json --warmups 0 --iterations 1
python tools/embeddinggemma2/video_compare.py --backend native \
  --corpus tools/embeddinggemma2/testdata/sampling/corpus.json \
  --model-dir .benchmark-assets/native-video/model \
  --binary zig/pkg/inference/zig-out/bin/antfly-inference-bench-server \
  --reference /tmp/sampling-pytorch.json --output /tmp/sampling-native.json \
  --warmups 0 --iterations 1 --concurrency 2 --sustained-rounds 2
```

Repeat the native command with `--backend metal` on an actual Metal host.
`video_sampling_errors.py` accepts the same corpus/model/binary/reference arguments
and checks malformed/empty windows, clean retries and ordered separate window
outputs. These are bounded correctness/operational checks. Latencies collected
under shared build load are not isolated performance benchmarks.


## Executed results

The [validation receipt](https://github.com/antflydb/antfly/blob/bf9d632d025a6b12837997f6aeb86e1a818ec831/zig/lib/video/testdata/video-sampling-validation.md)
records macOS CPU/Metal pretrained parity, actual Linux ARM64 portable execution,
HTTP policy rejection/retry and separate window outputs. `qualification.json`
contains source, artifact and clip hashes. `pytorch.json`, `native.json` and
`metal.json` retain complete vectors, frame selections and retrieval metrics.
`retry-oracle.json` preserves the exact earlier reference used by both HTTP
retry reports. General codec conformance, isolated performance measurements,
expanded display/Colour coverage and actual x86_64 runtime execution
remain outside this receipt's passing scope.


`linux-arm64-native.json` records the actual offline Linux pretrained run, including
all ten vectors, exact rankings/top-k and eight successful load requests at
concurrency two. `linux-arm64-server-build.log` records the static musl build.
The source is commit `98226fcb22`; the report binds its exact server binary and
the same checkpoint/reference as the macOS runs. The Linux container uses the
existing `antfly-pooling-qualification:latest` ARM64 image, overrides its entrypoint
with `python3`, mounts this worktree/model and the server readonly, and supplies a
writable result directory and tmpfs. Network is disabled; only local HTTP is used.
The `video_compare.py --backend native` command is identical except for Linux
paths. The PyTorch oracle remains the pinned CPU reference, rather than a separate
Linux PyTorch installation.
